summary: The statement and explicit tilt are proved without errors or gaps. The normalized factor slacks and positive barycentric coefficients exist because the origin is interior. Within a bin, all selected slack differences lie strictly between minus one and one. Applying the unique-interior-lattice-point hypothesis to both nonzero difference vectors forces the two omitted slack differences to have opposite signs and absolute values at least one. This gives the asserted opposite ordering and unit separation of rho and omega, hence total fractional slack at least m minus one at every point of a fiber of size m. The resulting fiber mass bound m times 2 to the power minus (m minus one) is at most one for every positive integer m, including singleton fibers. The tilt identity and finite-fiber comparison with the convergent positive series over the full nonnegative integer grid then give the strict bound 4 to the power r. Boundary support points, ties among maximal coefficients, and the smallest permitted factor dimensions cause no exceptions. Every use of the lattice concerns only differences in the original lattice, so no factorwise lattice splitting is assumed.
